headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Cursor’s shared filesystem/clipboard and MCP surfaces can ingest AutoGPT outputs, while AutoGPT can execute shell/network actions that amplify mistakes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists because AutoGPT can write files and use filesystem/agent protocol, while Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP inputs. If AutoGPT outputs attacker-controlled text into shared files or clipboard, Cursor may treat it as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes prompt-like content into a shared workspace file or clipboard
IF Cursor ingests that content through open buffers, clipboard, or MCP without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent
Require manual review of any AutoGPT-generated file before Cursor opens it
Turn off MCP servers for the shared workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT touches the filesystem and can egress to allowlisted network destinations; Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers/MCP servers. Shared local files or clipboard content can therefore leak from one agent into the other and onward to third parties in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local workspace or clipboard
IF Cursor forwards those contents to model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Use separate OS users or separate workspaces
Clear clipboard before switching agents
Restrict Cursor to a minimal project folder
Avoid placing secrets in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and Cursor can write files and modify git state while AutoGPT can use the filesystem. In a shared directory, concurrent edits and git operations can collide, causing lost work or corrupted state. Cursor’s per-window isolation still shares state via local filesystem, so the conflict remains.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs git writes or file writes without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Avoid Yolo mode during shared edits
requires-engineering: add file and git locking around both agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate files or outputs that Cursor may then read and act on through its agent loop, shell, or MCP tools. Because Cursor can execute commands and modify git state, an unverified AutoGPT mistake can cascade into irreversible repository changes or external actions. No built-in verification step is evident in either profile.
conditions: IF Cursor treats AutoGPT output as authoritative input
IF Cursor executes shell commands or commits based on that output without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before Cursor acts on AutoGPT output
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit checks
Disable auto-run/Yolo mode for the workflow
Limit Cursor to drafting only, not execution
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor explicitly touches clipboard contents, open files, and sends data to model providers/MCP servers, while AutoGPT can access files and network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is present in shared files or clipboard, it can flow into third-party services. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a general data-handling compliance risk rather than a specific breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in shared files or clipboard
IF Cursor forwards that data to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Disable clipboard sharing for sensitive sessions
Use a local-only model configuration where possible
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency boundary
